claims.claim: The query is ertugliflozin, a C-aryl glucoside SGLT2 inhibitor whose bridged dioxabicyclo[3.2.1]octane triol core closely matches tofogliflozin; tofogliflozin has human absolute oral bioavailability of about 97.5% measured by oral 20 mg dosing with concomitant IV microdosing, far above the 20% threshold.

Tofogliflozin mass-balance data show only 0.9% parent recovery in feces, indicating near-complete absorption, and animal F values of 85% in monkeys and 75% in mice support high oral bioavailability for this structural class.

For the close analog dapagliflozin, a 50 mg oral solution in healthy subjects gave at least 75% systemic absorption within 24 h based on urinary recovery of total radioactivity, and Caco-2 data show good permeability with only weak P-gp substrate activity (efflux ratio 3.8; weak substrate, not inhibitor), consistent with high F.
No affirmative query-specific low-F evidence is present; the L5 gut-wall efflux and intestinal-metabolism records are mechanistic and do not establish F < 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for ertugliflozin is present in the supplied records; the high prediction rests on the very close tofogliflozin analog and dapagliflozin absorption/permeability records.

No query-specific fasted-state PK record is supplied; the fasted condition is inferred to be compatible with the high tofogliflozin F and related SGLT2 fed/fasted AUC comparability, but not directly demonstrated.

L5 gut-wall efflux records are for dapagliflozin, not ertugliflozin; the efflux ratio 3.8 and P-gp substrate status are mechanistic and not quantitative F, and transferability to the bridged dioxabicyclo core is inferred.
No query-specific intestinal metabolism records are supplied; no affirmative low-F evidence is present.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high because the query is structurally very close to tofogliflozin, whose human absolute oral bioavailability is ~97.5% across multiple L1/L2 records, and L4/L5 add supportive absorption and permeability evidence from the close analog dapagliflozin (≥75% systemic absorption, good Caco-2 permeability, only weak P-gp substrate activity); L5 efflux records are mechanistic and do not provide affirmative evidence for F < 20%.
